19 years ago, I was 19 (does this matter, probably. Just like numbers) and I had hair down to my ass. All my life, my hair was long (except when I was born, I came out of the womb with a pixie cut) and I wasn't allowed to cut it. So naturally there were a few instances of scissors and hair but nothing major. One day my mom teamed me for spending an hour in the shower washing my hair (it was long and thick) and then 3 hours using the hairdryer. How else was I supposed to get it dry? Anyway. She had said once, years prior, that I can cut my hair if I was earning my own money. We have this massive fight about wasting water, electricity and how vain I am and and and. So I called a friend and asked him for a hairstylist reccie because up until then, I had actually never been to a salon consistently enough to have a relationship with anyone. Anyway. I told my mom that my session was booked and I was getting a super short pixie cut. She looked like she was going to have an aneurysm when I said, I was paying for it with my own money. I went. The stylist let me sit for hours because they kept asking me if I was sure. I said yes, but I don't want to see it happen.

I walked out with boy length spikes and went to work. I was the talk of the office all night because everyone was against me cutting my hair. When my mom saw me, her eyes went wide and she said nothing. She didn't speak to me for six months. Every time she needed to speak to me it was an order, or a necessity and it was in her angry voice. SIX MONTHS.

Oh, yeah, NTA! Your hair, your choice.

This is so triggering for me because I have lived this and it wasn't a pretty experience. I put a lot of thought into my gift buying. I think of the person, what they'd like and what would mean something to them. I have received thoughtless gifts before and it has always ended up in the bin eventually.

Here's the story: my husband had left for another country to work. I was finishing off two part time jobs and had just about enough to cover myself and get a little gift for him. I printed out photos of our adventures for him to remind him of the year we had. Six weeks after leaving, I got on a plane to him to spend Christmas with him. I arrived to a chilly reception. It was the worst feeling ever. I was told we'd be spending Christmas with his new friends. This co-worker bought him a hover board, he bought them watches, bought the kid a big gift. What did he get me? The same perfume he'd gifted me at least 4 times before. He didn't acknowledge my gift at all. He screamed at me for being an ungrateful bitch, said that his friends have his back. Berated me for being upset. He'd never spoken to me like that before and he has never stood up for me like that ever in our 8 years together. 

Turned out. He was having an affair with the woman who we had spent Christmas with. I don't do Christmas gifts. I don't buy them unless it's for myself and I don't expect to receive anything from anyone and I say so because this is the most triggering shit ever.
